subject: chemistry
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

learningObjectives.title: Atomic structure and the Periodic Table

questions.q: Which state change is described by the term sublimation?
options: A solid changing directly into a gas
A liquid changing into a gas
A gas changing into a liquid
A solid changing into a liquid
questions.explain: Sublimation is the direct change of a solid to a gas without passing through the liquid state.

questions.q: Using particle theory, what happens to the particles in a solid when it melts?
options: They gain energy and can move around and slide past each other
New particles are created inside the substance
They lose energy and vibrate more slowly
They join together to form covalent molecules
questions.explain: On melting, particles gain enough energy to overcome the forces holding them in fixed positions, so they can move past one another.

questions.q: A substance has a melting point of -7 degrees C and a boiling point of 59 degrees C. In which state is it at a room temperature of 25 degrees C?
options: Liquid
Solid
Gas
It cannot exist at that temperature
questions.explain: At 25 degrees C the substance is above its melting point but below its boiling point, so it is a liquid.

questions.q: What is an element?
options: A substance made of only one type of atom
Two or more substances chemically joined together
Two or more substances mixed but not joined
A substance that always contains oxygen
questions.explain: An element is a pure substance containing only one type of atom and cannot be broken down chemically.

questions.q: Which statement best describes a compound?
options: Two or more elements chemically combined in fixed proportions
Two or more elements simply mixed together
A substance containing a single type of atom
Particles of the same element in different states
questions.explain: A compound consists of different elements chemically bonded together in a fixed ratio.

questions.q: Which technique would you use to separate an insoluble solid from a liquid?
options: Filtration
Fractional distillation
Crystallisation
Chromatography
questions.explain: Filtration separates an insoluble solid (the residue) from a liquid (the filtrate).

questions.q: Fractional distillation separates a mixture of miscible liquids based on differences in their:
options: Boiling points
Colours
Densities
Solubilities in water
questions.explain: Fractional distillation relies on the liquids having different boiling points so they evaporate and condense at different temperatures.

questions.q: What is the relative charge of a proton?
questions.explain: A proton has a relative charge of +1, an electron -1 and a neutron 0.

questions.q: An atom contains 11 protons, 12 neutrons and 11 electrons. What is its mass number?
questions.explain: The mass number is the total of protons and neutrons: 11 + 12 = 23.

questions.q: Isotopes of the same element have the same number of protons but different numbers of:
options: Neutrons
Electrons
Protons
Occupied electron shells
questions.explain: Isotopes have identical proton numbers but different neutron numbers, giving them different mass numbers.

questions.q: Elements in the same group of the Periodic Table have the same number of:
options: Electrons in their outer shell
Protons in the nucleus
Neutrons in the nucleus
Occupied electron shells
questions.explain: Elements in a group share the same number of outer-shell electrons, which gives them similar chemical properties.

questions.q: What is the chemical formula of sulfuric acid?
options: H2SO4
HCl
HNO3
H2SO3
questions.explain: Sulfuric acid has the formula H2SO4.

questions.q: What is the relative formula mass (Mr) of calcium carbonate, CaCO3? (Ar: Ca = 40, C = 12, O = 16)
Which coefficients balance the equation __H2 + __O2 -> __H2O?
questions.explain: 2H2 + O2 -> 2H2O balances four hydrogen atoms and two oxygen atoms on each side.

questions.q: In the reaction Zn + 2HCl -> ZnCl2 + H2, how many moles of hydrochloric acid react with one mole of zinc?
questions.explain: The balanced equation shows a 1:2 ratio, so 1 mole of zinc reacts with 2 moles of HCl.

questions.q: Ionic bonding is formed by:
options: The transfer of electrons from a metal atom to a non-metal atom
The sharing of pairs of electrons between atoms
A sea of delocalised electrons around fixed atoms
The complete loss of protons from atoms
questions.explain: In ionic bonding, electrons are transferred from a metal to a non-metal, forming oppositely charged ions that attract.

questions.q: A covalent bond is best described as:
options: A shared pair of electrons between two atoms
A transfer of electrons between atoms
A sea of delocalised electrons
An attraction between oppositely charged ions
questions.explain: A covalent bond consists of a shared pair of electrons, usually between two non-metal atoms.

questions.q: Why do ionic compounds conduct electricity when molten but not when solid?
options: The ions are free to move when molten but held in fixed positions when solid
Electrons are released only when the compound is molten
Molten compounds gain extra protons
Solid ionic compounds contain no charged particles
questions.explain: Conduction needs mobile charged particles; ions can move only when the lattice is molten (or dissolved).

questions.q: Which statement correctly describes metallic bonding?
options: A lattice of positive metal ions surrounded by a sea of delocalised electrons
Shared pairs of electrons between neighbouring atoms
Oppositely charged ions attracting in a giant lattice
Neutral atoms held together by weak intermolecular forces
questions.explain: In a metal, positive ions are held together by electrostatic attraction to a sea of delocalised electrons.

questions.q: During electrolysis, towards which electrode do positive ions (cations) move?
options: The cathode, the negative electrode
The anode, the positive electrode
The electrolyte in the centre
They do not move at all
questions.explain: Positive ions are attracted to the negatively charged cathode, where they gain electrons (reduction).
